001: Ivan, hi. Do you know where the nearest pharmacy is around here?
Hi, Anna. There's one across the street, around the corner. Do you need something?
Yeah, my head has been hurting for the second day, I want to buy something for it.
Then you'd better go see a doctor first, rather than taking pills at random.
You're probably right. But I'll still stop by the pharmacy first anyway.
Okay, just don't buy any strong medicine without a prescription.
002: Dmitry, I have a fever and I feel weak. What should I do?
You need to stay home and call a doctor to come to the house.
Can I just go to the clinic instead?
You can, but with a fever it's better not to go outside.
Okay, then I'll call the reception desk and request a doctor.
Right. And don't forget to mention that your throat hurts.
003: Hello, I have an appointment with the therapist for ten o'clock.
Hello, yes, that's correct. Do you have your insurance card and passport with you?
Yes, here they are. Will it be a long wait?
About fifteen minutes, the doctor will be free and will call you in.
Thank you. Can I get my blood pressure measured in the meantime?
Of course, go sit over there, the nurse will help you.
004: Sergey, have you already gotten your tests done?
Not yet, I only made an appointment for tomorrow morning.
What do you need to get tested? Blood from a finger or from a vein?
From a vein, on an empty stomach. And also a urine test.
I see. And when will the results be ready?
They said in two days. Then I go back to the doctor with them.
005: Elena, I have an appointment with the eye doctor at three o'clock. Will you keep me company?
Of course, I will. What happened?
I've started seeing worse at a distance, especially in the evening.
Maybe you're just tired from the computer? You rest, and it'll go away.
I'd like to believe that. But it's better to get checked.
Agreed. Your eyesight is no joke, better not to put it off.
006: Hello, I need a prescription for blood pressure medicine.
Hello. Does your primary care doctor have the prescription?
Yes, I saw him yesterday, he said he would write it.
Great. Then go to his office, he's free right now.
Thank you very much. And is the pharmacy at the hospital open?
Yes, it's open until eight in the evening, so you'll make it in time.
007: Maria, do you know where I can get a flu shot?
I do, at the clinic on the first floor, in the vaccination room.
Do I need to make an appointment in advance?
No, they usually see people on a first-come, first-served basis.
Don't be scared, it's quicker than a mosquito bite.
008: Dmitry, how did your appointment with the surgeon go?
Fine. He looked at my leg and said it's a sprain.
And what did he prescribe? Ointments, pills?
An ointment and rest for a week. Plus compresses.
Good that it's nothing serious. And do you need to get dressings changed?
Yes, every other day, I signed up at the dressing room.
009: Hello, could you tell me, do you have anything for a cough?
Hello. Do you need syrup or tablets?
Syrup is better, it's easier for me to take.
Here's a good option with herbs. But first, read the instructions.
Of course. And how much does it cost?
Four hundred and fifty rubles. Should I package it for you?
010: Olga, you look tired. Are you sick?
Yeah, a little. Yesterday I had a fever all evening.
No, I took some fever reducer and went to bed.
Next time, definitely go see a doctor, okay?
Okay, I promise. If I don't feel better tomorrow, I'll go to the clinic.
